tagline: Live public data, presented so you can trust it: every tool fetches from the source API in your browser, and every chart declares what one row counts, what it cannot answer, and which framing choices were made. Adding a dataset is one JSON file. Adding a tool is one HTML file and one manifest line.

tools.badge: For customers · live, fetches the city's API
tools.title: What does that grade in the window actually mean?
tools.blurb: Type any NYC restaurant. See the score, this restaurant's own history, and what the inspector actually found — because a good number and a fixed building are not the same thing.

tools.badge: For the business · live, fetches the city's API
tools.title: You failed the inspection. What do you fix first?
tools.blurb: Your open violations, ranked by how often that exact code was still there at the re-inspection. Measured across 6,960 paired NYC inspections — so the order is evidence, not a guess about what looks worst.

tools.badge: For both · the address they share — 3 city datasets on the tax lot
tools.title: What does the building say?
tools.blurb: City rodent inspections and 311 complaints at a restaurant's tax lot — labeled building-level, because 46.4% of NYC restaurants share their lot with another restaurant and the record may belong to a neighbour. Every restaurant page links here on its address.

tools.title: Who else does the city inspect?
tools.blurb: Restaurants hang a grade in the window. Barbershops, pools, daycares, car washes and tax preparers are inspected too — the results are public and almost nobody reads them.

tools.title: Watch a true chart become a false one
tools.blurb: One chart, pinned to your screen, spun one display lever at a time. No number changes at any point — that is the lesson.

tools.badge: The talk · how this app gets presented
tools.title: How do you demo this in five sentences?
tools.blurb: The demo-day storyboard: a person before the product, one sentence per beat, the product not named until Beat 4 — with the live captures, the runbook, and the fallback protocol. All six storyboard gates pass on these exact sentences.
